title: Hardik Pandya Trade Back on Table as Franchise Makes Fresh Inquiry
excerpt: Cricbuzz reports renewed franchise interest in the Mumbai Indians captain, with the next three to four weeks likely decisive — but MI publicly insists no trade talks are on until its post-season review is done.
body:
• Cricbuzz reports that Hardik Pandya is attracting renewed IPL trade interest, with at least one franchise making fresh inquiries to Mumbai Indians — and something concrete could take shape in the next three to four weeks.
  • Mumbai Indians have not committed either way: an MI official told Sportstar the franchise is "not engaged in conversations with regard to player trades" until its post-season review is complete.
  • Chennai Super Kings and Kolkata Knight Riders are among the franchises MI has held discussions with; Lucknow Super Giants and Rajasthan Royals have also been linked, though those remain at rumour stage.
  • The clock is tight: retention deadline is November 15 ahead of the mid-December auction in Goa, and fitness is a live question — Pandya is injured and out of India's A-team ODI series against Australia starting October 6.

The Hardik Pandya trade saga is stirring again. After a lull in which Mumbai Indians insisted nothing was on the table, Cricbuzz reports that at least one IPL franchise has made fresh inquiries about the Mumbai Indians captain — and that the next three to four weeks could decide the all-rounder's future before the IPL 2027 cycle is set. For a player who has dominated the IPL trade conversation like no other over the past year, this is the first genuine forward motion in months.

Context & Background

Pandya, 32, rejoined Mumbai Indians in 2024 in the most contentious move of recent IPL history, replacing Rohit Sharma as captain after leading Gujarat Titans to the 2022 title in their debut season and the 2023 final the year after. The Mumbai homecoming has not delivered: MI finished last in 2024, reached Qualifier 2 in 2025 before falling to Punjab Kings, and ended ninth in 2026. His own numbers tell the split story franchises must now weigh — fewer than 225 runs at an average below 25 in each of the last three seasons, but at a strike rate close to 150, alongside 29 wickets. In IPL 2026 alone: 10 matches, 206 runs, 4 wickets at an economy of 11.42. He has not played competitive cricket since the IPL ended, is currently at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru working back to fitness, and a recent injury has ruled him out of the India A ODI series against Australia beginning October 6.

Impact & Analysis

The market dynamics explain why this is both hot and slow. MI sources indicate the all-rounder may not be traded at all, even as Cricbuzz understands calls have gone back and forth between franchises and the MI management. Kolkata Knight Riders have expressed interest but are not prepared to include key players in any trade package — the stumbling block that has stalled things at the preliminary stage. The CSK door may have cooled: with Zaheer Khan now at the helm there, and a complicated history between him and Pandya from their time together at MI, the general impression is that a Chennai move has receded, though Cricbuzz notes professional equations can change. Fitness shadows everything: Gautam Gambhir has emphasised how much India need a fully fit Pandya for next year's World Cup, which makes any buying franchise bet on the GT version of the player rather than the struggling MI version. The timeline is structural, not negotiable — the retention deadline is November 15, the mid-December auction is in Goa, and while the trading window stays open until a month before the season, franchises plan their season through retentions and releases.

"Our post-season review is currently on, and we are looking into all aspects of the team. Contrary to reports, we are not engaged in conversations with regard to player trades; the same is only possible once the review is complete."

— Mumbai Indians franchise official, to Sportstar

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora's IPL audience — the US watch parties, the Dubai fantasy leagues, the Toronto office group chats — a Pandya trade would redraw the season's loyalties overnight. He is one of the few players whose franchise shirt genuinely moves sentiment across continents, and wherever he lands, that team's diaspora fanbase changes. The betting among Indian-origin fans this week is less about money than about fit: which version of Pandya turns up, and in which colours.

What's Next

The decisive window is the next three to four weeks, when retentions crystallise and franchises must lock their plans for the Goa auction. Watch for three signals: whether MI's post-season review produces a leadership decision — speculation has swirled around Tilak Varma as a possible future captain — whether KKR softens on its trade package, and whether Pandya clears the fitness tests at the Centre of Excellence. If none of those break, the most likely outcome is the one MI already hints at: the most valuable trade chip in the league stays put, at least for now.
